title: RAW UNREVIEWED: one named object shown in two keyed views
summary: A public primary might depict the same explicitly titled object in two labeled views, such as outside and cutaway, while naming features unique to each view. The source's own cross-reference would own object identity independently of visual guesswork. A proposed Voynich reading would have to keep the object term stable while accounting for view-specific terms across complete admitted records. A merely similar drawing or an inferred plant identity does not qualify; source and target capacity remain unknown.

design.mechanism: source-declared cross-view identity separates object name from view-dependent feature names
design.unit: paired source views and full admitted target records
design.contrast: stable object plus changed feature wording versus two unrelated scene labels
design.prediction: a predeclared whole-form mapping keeps the owner term invariant across both views and confines different forms to source-keyed features
